question:
Diameter \(ACE\) is divided at \(C\) in the ratio \(2:3.\) The two semicircles, \(ABC\) and \(CDE,\) divide the circular region into an upper (shaded) region and a lower region. The ratio of the area of the upper region to that of the lower region is

[Figure 1](figures/1997_AMC_8_Q24_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The shaded region can be built from three semicircles: start with the upper half of the large circle, remove semicircle \(ABC\), and add semicircle \(CDE\).

[Figure 1](figures/1997_AMC_8_Q24_question_fig1.svg)

Choose a length unit so that \(AC=4\) and \(CE=6\), which preserves the given ratio \(2:3\). Then \(AE=10\), so the three radii are \(2\), \(3\), and \(5\). Changing the measurement unit does not change the ratio of the two areas.

A semicircle of radius \(r\) has area \(\frac12\pi r^2\). Thus the shaded area is
\[
\frac{25\pi}{2}-\frac{4\pi}{2}+\frac{9\pi}{2}=15\pi.
\]
The whole circle has area \(25\pi\), so the lower region has area \(25\pi-15\pi=10\pi\). Therefore the requested ratio is
\[
15\pi:10\pi=\boxed{3:2},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
